marks.gloss_en: אף על גב דטבא היא לדידיה... השתא מיהא רעה היא -- though good for him, now at any rate it is bad
what is the case? e.g. where a dam burst onto his land
the mishnah (cited as lemma): one blesses over the bad [in the manner of blessing over the good]
דלא ליפתח פומיה לשטן, דאמר ריש לקיש וכן תנא משמיה דרבי יוסי: לעולם אל יפתח אדם פיו לשטן
Abaye: a person should not say so [read: the clause 'if ruin befalls me'], so as not to open his mouth to the Satan
מאי קראה? כמעט כסדם היינו... מאי אהדר להו נביא: שמעו דבר ה' קציני סדם -- they compared themselves to Sodom, and the prophet answered them as rulers of Sodom
Rav Yosef: what is the verse? 'we were almost as Sodom, we were like Gomorrah' (Isa 1:9); what did the prophet answer them? 'hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom' (Isa 1:10)

R' Abbahu entered a bathhouse; it gave way beneath him; a miracle was done for him -- he stood on a pillar and saved a hundred and one men with one arm. He said: היינו דרב אחא -- this is [the case of] Rav Acha's thanks for being saved from the fire
דתני דבי רבי ישמעאל: ורפא ירפא -- מכאן שניתנה רשות לרופא לרפאות
Abaye: a person should not say so [read: 'it is not the way of people to heal', the clause his proof bears on]
on his entering, what does he say? 'may it be Your will, Lord my God, that You bring me into this city in peace'
first version, Rav Mattana: they taught this only of a city where they do not judge and execute
latter version, Rav Mattana: even in a city where they judge and execute [he says the prayers]

one entering the bathhouse says: 'may it be Your will, Lord my God, that You save me from this and its like, and let no ruin or iniquity befall me; and if ruin or iniquity befalls me, may my death be atonement for all my iniquities'
when he comes out, what does he say? Rav Acha: 'I thank You, Lord, that You saved me from the fire'

Rav Acha: one entering to let blood says: 'may it be Your will, Lord my God, that this undertaking be for healing for me, and heal me, for You are a faithful God of healing and Your healing is true, since it is not the way of people to heal, but they have become accustomed'
when he stands up [after bloodletting], what does he say? Rav Acha: 'Blessed... who heals for nothing'
דאפילו קנה ויש לו אין צריך לברך, וכל שכן קנה וחזר וקנה דאין צריך לברך -- per R' Meir: if even one who has the like and buys need not bless, all the more one who bought and bought again

אמר לך רבי יוחנן: הוא הדין דלרבי יהודה קנה וחזר וקנה נמי צריך לברך -- R' Yochanan accords with R' Yehuda after all (= p_hu_hadin_ryehuda); the dispute was placed at 'has the like' to show R' Meir's strength (= p_lehodiacha_kocho_rmeir)
per R' Yehuda, the same law: one who bought and bought again also must bless
מכלל -- R' Yochanan's 'even' stops at 'has the like', and Rav Huna exempts even that; so bought-and-bought-again is exempt on both
it follows [on the first version] that where he bought and bought again, all agree he need not bless
מכלל -- Rav Huna exempts only bought-and-bought-again, and R' Yochanan requires even that; so 'has the like and bought' requires a blessing on both
latter version, Rav Huna: where he bought and bought again, he need not bless

מיתיבי (the R' Meir / R' Yehuda baraita)... אלא ללישנא בתרא, רבי יוחנן דאמר כמאן? לא כרבי מאיר ולא כרבי יהודה! -- the tannaim dispute only 'has the like'; neither speaks of bought and bought again requiring a blessing (60a.4)
R' Meir: one who built a new house or bought new vessels and has none like them must bless
וליפלגו בקנה וחזר וקנה דאין צריך לברך, להודיעך כחו דרבי יהודה! -- then let them dispute bought-and-bought-again, to show R' Yehuda's strength
כח דהתירא עדיף ליה -- the strength of permission is preferable to him (= p_koach_deheteira_adif)
the strength of permission is preferable to him
on the first version, Rav Huna accords with R' Meir
שנאמר: ותקרא את שמה דינה
ולא מהני רחמי? מתיב רב יוסף: ואחר ילדה בת... -- by Rav's exposition, Leah's judgment turned the male fetus into a daughter; so prayer does help
אין מזכירין מעשה נסים -- one does not cite a miraculous event [as evidence]

Rav: 'afterward' (Gen 30:21) means after Leah passed judgment on herself -- twelve tribes are to come from Jacob, six have come from me and four from the maidservants, that is ten; if this one is male my sister Rachel will not be even as one of the maidservants -- at once [the fetus] was turned into a daughter
כדתניא: משלשה ועד ארבעים יבקש רחמים שיהא זכר -- within forty days prayer for a male is still in place
ואיבעית אימא: מעשה דלאה בתוך ארבעים יום הוה -- Leah's episode was within forty days, when prayer for a male is still in place (= p_leah_toch_arbaim)
the stam: Leah's episode was within forty days [of conception]
שנאמר: אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר
ומי מהני רחמי? והאמר רב יצחק בריה דרב אמי: איש מזריע תחלה יולדת נקבה, אשה מזריעה תחלה יולדת זכר -- the sex is already determined, so how can prayer [within forty days] help?
הכא במאי עסקינן -- כגון שהזריעו שניהם בבת אחת: where both emitted at once, [and prayer can still decide] (= p_okimta_bevat_achat)
Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Ami: if the man emits seed first, she bears a female; if the woman emits seed first, she bears a male
the mishnah: one whose wife was pregnant and he said 'may it be [Your] will that she bear [a male]' -- this is a vain prayer
אף על גב דרעה היא לדידיה... השתא מיהא טובה היא -- though bad for him, now at any rate it is good
what is the case? e.g. where he found a lost object
the mishnah (cited as lemma): and over the good [one blesses in the manner of blessing over the bad]
ועליו הכתוב אומר: משמועה רעה לא יירא נכון לבו בטוח בה׳
Hillel the Elder was coming on the road and heard a scream in the city; he said: I am sure this is not in my house
דכתיב: פחדו בציון חטאים
והכתיב: אשרי אדם מפחד תמיד -- Scripture praises one who fears always; how is fear a mark of a sinner?
ההוא בדברי תורה כתיב -- that verse is written of words of Torah (= p_ryby_bedivrei_torah)
R' Yishmael son of R' Yosei, seeing [the disciple] afraid, said to him: you are a sinner
דכתיב: כי פחד פחדתי ויאתיני ואשר יגרתי יבא לי
והא כתיב: אשרי אדם מפחד תמיד -- Scripture praises one who fears always
ההוא בדברי תורה כתיב -- that verse is written of words of Torah (= p_rh_bedivrei_torah)
[Yehuda bar Natan] sighed; [Rav Hamnuna] said to him: does that man want to bring suffering upon himself?
